title: Steering Column Shroud Removal and Installation
introduction:
The steering column shrouds form the fitted shell around the column and its nearby controls. Their tidy appearance hides several different attachments: the upper gap hider, tabs reached by turning the wheel, outer clips and screws underneath. I treat the shell like a jacket with concealed fasteners—finding the closures beats tugging harder on the sleeves.

This procedure removes and refits the trim around the column. The illustrations show the left-hand-drive arrangement, with right-hand drive treated as similar. Use the wheel positions and highlighted attachment locations to navigate the sequence; this job does not call for disconnecting the steering shaft or removing the steering wheel.

items.name: Prevent an unexpected start
items.detail: Park on level ground with the parking brake applied and wheels chocked; keep P selected on an automatic or a parked gear on a manual. Disable remote start, if equipped, through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before dismantling anything. Otherwise, someone could remotely start the car, causing personal injury or death. If the setting needs ignition power, select engine-off ON from confirmed OFF by pressing START/STOP without pressing either pedal; if already ON with the engine stopped, retain ON. After the setting change, return ON to OFF without pressing a pedal; if already OFF, leave OFF. Keep the engine stopped throughout. Retain the valid intelligent access key inside only for the mechanical column positioning and wheel rotations described below; keep ignition OFF throughout the trim work. With ignition OFF, remove the key when the mechanical wheel movements and refitting are finished; this procedure does not disturb switches or their terminals. An accidental start during service can cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Personal protection
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection while servicing the vehicle. Wear protective gloves when handling pointed or sharp edges. Failure to follow these precautions may result in serious personal injury.

items.name: Prepare the listed equipment
items.detail: Have an interior trim remover for the gap hider and a flat-bladed screwdriver for the wheel-accessible shroud tabs. The lower shroud also has screws; their drive type and tightening specification are not stated.

items.name: Work through the attachment layers
items.detail: Make room by extending and lowering the column before releasing trim. Remove the upper gap-hider attachment and upper shroud before removing the lower shroud screws.

edits.text: NOTE: The illustrations show LHD (left-hand drive); RHD (right-hand drive) is similar.
edits.why: Use the illustrated relationship between the wheel, shrouds and attachments while allowing for the opposite driving position.

edits.text: Fully extend the steering column toward you and lower it.
edits.why: With ignition OFF, retain the valid intelligent access key inside for mechanical shroud access: entering with it unlocks an equipped steering-wheel lock. If the wheel cannot rotate, do not force it or switch ignition ON around exposed parts; stop for the matching steering-lock instructions. The adjustment lever is beneath the column. Lower it to release the adjustment, fully extend and lower the column, then raise the lever to secure that working position.

edits.text:
Use the Interior Trim Remover to release the tabs attaching the upper gap hider to the upper steering column shroud. Disconnect the gap hider from the shroud and position it aside.
Use the General Equipment: Interior Trim Remover
edits.why: The gap hider bridges the space between the instrument-panel area and the upper shroud. The close-up locates its tabbed attachment along the upper edge of the shroud; the arrows show the gap hider lifting away there. Free that edge before moving it aside so it no longer ties the upper shroud to the surrounding trim.

edits.text: Release the upper steering column shroud tabs using the wheel positions below.
edits.why: Turning the wheel exposes the tab locations behind it in succession. These tabs are released before the outer side clips and upper shroud are removed.

edits.text:
Rotate the steering wheel 90 degrees to the first illustrated position. Use the Flat-Bladed Screwdriver to release the steering column shroud tab exposed behind the wheel.
Use the General Equipment: Flat-Bladed Screwdriver
edits.why: The first view shows the wheel turned to uncover the tab location on one side of the column. Place the screwdriver at that exposed attachment; the wheel rotation creates access rather than removing the shroud by itself.

edits.text:
From the preceding position, rotate the steering wheel 180 degrees in the opposite direction to the next illustrated position. Use the Flat-Bladed Screwdriver to release the other steering column shroud tab.
Use the General Equipment: Flat-Bladed Screwdriver
edits.why: The next view exposes the attachment on the opposite side. Read this as the next movement in the sequence, not a new starting position measured from straight ahead. The drawings locate the screwdriver access points without specifying a tab-deflection direction.

edits.text: Release the outer clips on each side of the upper steering column shroud, then lift the upper shroud off.
edits.why: The upward arrow shows the removal movement, and the detached-part view locates clip features along the shroud’s side edges. With the wheel-accessible tabs already released and the gap hider aside, these outer clips are the remaining attachments identified for the upper piece.

edits.text: Remove the screws securing the lower steering column shroud, then remove the lower shroud.
edits.why: The underside view identifies the screw positions: one is recessed in a deeper access opening, while another is visible in the shallower opening. I use that view to find the attachments before trying to move the lower shell. No screw tightening torque is stated.

edits.text: Install in reverse removal order. Position the lower steering column shroud and reinstall its screws. Fit the upper shroud, engage its outer side clips and re-engage the tabs reached through the steering-wheel positions. Reattach the upper gap hider to the upper shroud. Restore the column adjustment and secure its adjustment lever.
edits.why: Work from the lower shell back to the upper shell and gap hider so each attachment returns to its original partner. Check that the tabs and clips are engaged and the trim is seated. The steering-wheel movements provide access to the same tab locations during refitting; they do not create an additional steering-system repair. Reverse the access wheel rotations to restore its position, keeping ignition OFF and the valid key inside. Release the column-adjustment lever before restoring the column position, then raise the lever to lock it. Check that the refitted shells are seated, every released attachment is engaged and the column remains securely adjusted. Clear the tools, confirm ignition OFF and remove the key. This is a trim-refitting check, not a steering-system diagnosis.

editorialRevision.scope: Owner-backed stationary known-state preparation and mechanical steering-lock/column-adjustment coordination, with explicit equipment names and final trim retention check. No primary action text, figures or specifications changed.
